purpose: Rc process-graph parity matrix for Star 9
rule: Pipelines, jobs, rfork, notes, and wait must be represented through Star 9 tasks, fd tables, pipes, namespaces, env files, and device files. Host shell side channels are not acceptable.

layers.portable_evaluator: crates/star9-rc keeps deterministic captured execution for fake hosts, pure built-ins, browser-limited hosts, and hosts without a streaming execution provider.
layers.star9_adapter: crates/star9-shell/src/rc.rs implements process-graph hooks over Star 9 task, fd, pipe, namespace, and execution-registry surfaces.
layers.provider_execution: Native-host Star 9 rc can execute external WASI stages and opt-in native stages through provider-backed task/fd graphs. JS/WASM worker graph execution remains a browser/runtime-port provider boundary.

features.notes: The reusable rc crate exposes host-neutral graph specs and records without depending on Star 9 runtime types.
The Star 9 adapter creates per-stage task records, standard fds, and selected pipe fd bindings under .rc/graphs.

Native-host rc starts two-stage and linear multi-stage WASI pipelines plus opt-in native stages concurrently, installs pipe/file/stdio descriptors into task fd tables, closes writer endpoints for EOF, reads final stdout/stderr from task fds, and aggregates pipeline status. JS/WASM worker stages still fall back unless a browser/runtime provider handles them.
<{} and >{} remain evaluator data paths for portability, while the Star 9 adapter creates task/fd graph records that expose the intended pipe endpoint.

Pure built-ins keep deterministic job records. External WASI/native graph jobs can run in provider threads and wait through rc job ids. Persistent task-group files and cleanup controls remain future depth.

Captured stdout/stderr redirection, fd dup/close, process-substitution sink handling, and provider stdio descriptor installation are implemented. Full arbitrary fd graph streaming for every rc edge form remains future precision work.
rfork e is accepted through the host boundary. Namespace/env/fd/process-group sharing flags remain precisely rejected until Star 9 has matching task scope controls.
sigexit and rc note functions work. The Star 9 adapter broadcasts notes through #signal/data when present. Delivery into active provider-backed task groups remains future work.
Browser rc keeps deterministic evaluator behavior unless a worker-backed task/fd graph provider is explicitly added. Raw native process semantics are not a browser capability.

import! services use cross-document MessagePort 9P. ws!/wss! services can be mounted through a configured WebSocket 9P provider. webtransport! addresses parse and route through the same provider hook, but the default SystemElement reports WebTransport provider-missing until a concrete provider is installed.
